title: Stream surface simplifier: harmonize auth cache + introduce retry blueprints across SDKs
author: Priya Nambiar
release_notes: Harmonize token caching and add Retry Blueprints + new StreamSurface helper. Bump SDK versions: Python v2.4.0, TypeScript v1.31.0, Go v1.12.0. No user-visible breaking changes; migration notes added to docs.
commits: a1f4c3e: introduce TokenProvider interface and centralized cache adapter
b2e7a9d: add retry-blueprint compiler and 3 built-in presets (latency, durability, conservative)
c3d9f88: StreamSurface helper for annotated backpressure hints and resume-friendly cursors
d4a02b1: TS/PY/GO SDK integrations and examples + version bumps
e5b33f2: tests + e2e (stream handshake + reauth) and docs
files_changed: ci/pipeline-sdk-tests.yml: add matrix for blueprint presets
description:
Context and motivation: We observed multiple customer issues where mid-stream credential swaps and subtle TTL drift caused spurious reauths and duplicated upstream calls. The three language SDKs were each handling token caching slightly differently and had scattered backpressure primitives. This PR consolidates the token cache backing into a single TokenProvider abstraction, introduces a small Retry Blueprint compiler (opinionated presets) for common LLM inference patterns, and surfaces a StreamSurface helper to make backpressure and resume behavior ergonomic across SDKs.

What this PR does (high level):
- Adds TokenProvider interface (py/ts/go) and a centralized cache adapter that normalizes TTL windows and clock skew tolerance. SDKs now prefer the TokenProvider and fall back to existing per-call hooks while emitting deprecation warnings.
- Introduces Retry Blueprint DSL and compiler with three built-in presets: latency-optimized, durability-optimized, and conservative. Blueprints are serializable JSON objects that map to SDK-friendly retry stacks.
- Adds StreamSurface helper: a small runtime shim that attaches transparent resume cursors, exposes backpressureHint() for producers, and coordinates graceful reauth mid-stream without losing already emitted chunks.
- Integrates changes into all three SDKs and bumps versions (py 2.4.0, ts 1.31.0, go 1.12.0).
- Adds e2e tests covering: continuous streaming with token rotation, retry-blueprint application under transient errors, and pause/resume semantics with StreamSurface.

Checklist: 
- [x] TokenProvider interface (py/ts/go)
- [x] Central cache adapter + TTL harmonization
- [x] Retry Blueprint compiler + presets
- [x] StreamSurface shim + cross-SDK examples
- [x] Unit and e2e tests
- [x] Docs and migration guide added
- [x] Version bumps for all SDKs

Commit summary: a1f4c3e introduces the TokenProvider and cache semantics; b2e7a9d adds the retry-blueprint compiler and basic presets; c3d9f88 implements StreamSurface shims; d4a02b1 wires the pieces into each SDK and increments versions; e5b33f2 contains tests and docs.

Files changed (high level): see list above. Notable small API surfaces:
- TokenProvider.get_token(expiry_buffer_ms?: number) -> returns token + expiry metadata
- RetryBlueprint.compile(presetName | config) -> RetryPolicy object for internal runner
- StreamSurface.observe(stream, opts) -> returns resumeHandle { cursor, meta } and backpressureHint(lp)

Review conversation (condensed, chronological):
- Jonah Miller: "Nice consolidation. Two asks: (1) add an explicit clock-skew tolerance constant and expose it for enterprise deployers; (2) can we make the conservative preset explicitly capped retries for idempotent reranks?"
- Priya (author): "Added CLOCK_SKEW_MS setting with env override and updated conservative preset to cap to 3 retries for idempotent ops. See commit b2e7a9d and tests/e2e coverage."
- Eva Schultz: "TS surface looks good, but I saw a flaky test in the initial CI run for stream resume on Node 18 matrix. Can you stabilize?"
- Priya: "Root cause was a race in the test harness; introduced deterministic fake clock in tests and re-ran CI."
- Marco Ruiz: "Docs are solid. One suggestion: a short migration note calling out deprecation window for per-call hooks."
- Priya: "Added migration note and deprecation warnings (90-day window)."
- Jonah Miller: "Approve after CI green."

CI history: initial run: pipeline-sdk-tests matrix flagged flaky stream_resume.test on ts/node18 (timeout). After adding deterministic fake clock and slight test timeout increase, rerun passed. Full e2e matrix passed (py 3.11, ts node 18/20, go 1.20).

Backwards compatibility and migration notes: This change is intentionally non-breaking. Existing per-call auth hooks remain supported but will log a one-time deprecation warning. The TokenProvider is recommended for all new integrations and unlocks consistent TTL behavior across SDKs. Retry Blueprints are opt-in; default SDK behavior unchanged until a blueprint is passed to the client config.

Testing and validation: Added ~40 unit tests across SDKs (cache edge cases, blueprint compile paths, stream resume semantics) and 6 e2e scenarios in CI. Local performance run shows no observable token fetch latency regression (~+2% median on small benchmark, within noise).

Merge outcome: Squash merged to main after approvals from Jonah and Eva and CI green. Changelog and migration docs published to docs/sdk-migration/auth-cache-and-retry-blueprints.md.

Follow-ups / TODOs:
- Track telemetry (ENG-2145) to monitor customer toggles of TokenProvider.
- Consider a lightweight server-side blueprint registry for sharing presets across teams.

Related work: references ENG-2145, ENG-2201. See also earlier PRs on session bridges and stream ergonomics for context.

merge_commit_message:
squash: harmonize token caching, add retry blueprints and StreamSurface across SDKs

- TokenProvider abstraction
- Retry blueprint compiler + presets
- StreamSurface helper and cross-SDK integrations
- Version bumps: py v2.4.0, ts v1.31.0, go v1.12.0
notes: No runtime configuration changes required for current users
Migration guide added to docs, includes sample TokenProvider adapter and blueprint JSON examples
Deprecation: per-call auth hooks will be removed after 90 days - deprecation warnings emitted now
